card.text: Lebanon first went to the Olympics in 1948. Four years later in Helsinki, two Greco-Roman wrestlers won medals on the same day: Zakaria Chihab took silver in the bantamweight class (57 kg), and Khalil Taha took bronze at welterweight (73 kg). They were Lebanon's first Olympic medals.

caption:
From the archive: Helsinki, 1952. 🤼

Lebanon's first Olympic medals came on the wrestling mat. At the Helsinki Games, Zakaria Chihab won silver and Khalil Taha bronze in Greco-Roman wrestling, both on the same day.

Lebanon has won four Olympic medals in all, the most recent in 1980.

Spot the "LIBAN" tracksuits in the crowd. 🇱🇧

📸 Hugo Sundström / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 4.0 (wrestling at Helsinki, 20 July 1952)
Source: Olympics.com, Olympedia

alt: Archive cover, Helsinki 1952: Lebanon's first Olympic medals. Two wrestlers, two medals: Zakaria Chihab won silver and Khalil Taha bronze. 74 years ago. Sepia photo of wrestling at the Helsinki Games on 20 July 1952, with spectators in LIBAN tracksuits in the foreground.

The story: Lebanon first went to the Olympics in 1948. In Helsinki in 1952, two Greco-Roman wrestlers won medals on the same day: Zakaria Chihab silver at bantamweight (57 kg) and Khalil Taha bronze at welterweight (73 kg), Lebanon's first Olympic medals.

Lebanon's Olympic medals: Zakaria Chihab, wrestling, Helsinki 1952, silver; Khalil Taha, wrestling, Helsinki 1952, bronze; Kheir Mohamed Tarabulsi, weightlifting, Munich 1972, silver; Hassan Bchara, wrestling, Moscow 1980, bronze. 4 Olympic medals in all.
Then and now: 1952, two medals on one day in Helsinki, Lebanon's first; 1980, Hassan Bchara's bronze in Moscow is still Lebanon's most recent Olympic medal.

facts.claim: Lebanon's first Olympic Games were London 1948 (the NOC's first)

Helsinki 1952: Zakaria Chihab silver, Greco-Roman bantamweight (57 kg); Khalil Taha bronze, Greco-Roman welterweight (73 kg); both won on the same day; 2 medals; Lebanon's first Olympic medals (Taha 'Lebanon's second Olympic medalist'); 2026 - 1952 = 74 years

Lebanon's 4 Olympic medals: Chihab silver 1952, Taha bronze 1952, Kheir Mohamed Tarabulsi (Olympics.com spelling; Olympedia writes Mohamed Kheir Tarabulsi) silver in weightlifting (men's 75 kg) at Munich 1972, Hassan Bchara bronze in Greco-Roman wrestling (+100 kg) at Moscow 1980; 1980 is the most recent
